messages.content: "Can you help me book a ticket for a concert of Taylor Swift in New York with a VIP Seating add-on, then book another ticket for a concert of Ed Sheeran in Los Angeles with a Backstage Pass and Parking Pass add-ons, and finally book a ticket for the Coachella festival in Indio with a Camping Pass and Parking Pass add-ons?"

function.name: concert_book_ticket
function.description: Book a ticket for a concert at a specific location with various add-ons like backstage pass. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: Name of the artist for the concert.

location.description: City where the concert will take place.

add_ons.description: Add-ons for the concert. Default is 'VIP Seating' if not specified.

function.name: festival_book_ticket
function.description: Book a ticket for a festival at a specific location with various add-ons like camping access. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City where the festival will take place.

add_ons.description: Add-ons for the festival. Default is 'Camping Pass' if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants multiple bookings:

1. Concert: Taylor Swift, New York, add_on: VIP Seating (default is VIP Seating anyway).
2. Concert: Ed Sheeran, Los Angeles, add_ons: Backstage Pass and Parking Pass. The function signature expects add_ons?: "Backstage Pass" | "VIP Seating" | "Parking Pass"[]; but it's ambiguous: It says add_ons? can be one of those strings or an array? Actually type says add_ons?: "Backstage Pass" | "VIP Seating" | "Parking Pass"[], which seems wrong: maybe they intended union of string or array. But we need to provide correct format. We should give array of strings: ["Backstage Pass", "Parking Pass"].

3. Festival: Coachella, Indio, add_ons: Camping Pass and Parking Pass. So add_ons: ["Camping Pass", "Parking Pass"].

We need to call the function twice: first concert_book_ticket for Taylor Swift, second concert_book_ticket for Ed Sheeran, third festival_book_ticket for Coachella.

But the system instruction says: "When calling a function, do not mention the function name or arguments in your response." That means we cannot say "Sure, here's the booking details" etc. We just output the function calls as JSON objects. Also we must separate them into separate messages. So we need to produce three messages, each containing a single function call. Each message must contain only the function call JSON object. No other text.

Thus we produce:

Message 1: {"name":"concert_book_ticket","arguments":{"artist":"Taylor Swift","location":"New York"}}

Message 2: {"name":"concert_book_ticket","arguments":{"artist":"Ed Sheeran","location":"Los Angeles","add_ons":["Backstage Pass","Parking Pass"]}}

Message 3: {"name":"festival_book_ticket","arguments":{"festival":"Coachella","location":"Indio","add_ons":["Camping Pass","Parking Pass"]}}

We must ensure no extra keys. For the first, we don't specify add_ons because default is VIP Seating. Good.

Return these as separate messages.
